title: A separable quadratic completion splits geometrically
statement: Let $k$ be a field, $S$ a finitely generated $k$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra], $\mathfrak p\subset S$ a maximal ideal, $A=S_{\mathfrak p}$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], and $F=S/\mathfrak p$ finite separable over $k$ [def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension]. Write $\widehat A$ for the maximal-ideal-adic completion [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. Suppose there are a $k$-algebra section $\sigma:F\to\widehat A$ of the residue map and a continuous complete local $F$-algebra isomorphism $\widehat A\cong F[[u,v]]/(Q)$ inducing the identity on $F$, where $F$ acts through $\sigma$, $Q=au^2+buv+cv^2$, $a,b,c\in F$, and $b^2-4ac\ne0$ [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series]. For every algebraic closure $\Omega/k$ [def-weil-algebraic-closure] and every $k$-embedding $\iota:F\hookrightarrow\Omega$, let $\mathfrak q$ be the kernel of $S\otimes_k\Omega\to\Omega$, $s\otimes\lambda\mapsto\iota(\bar s)\lambda$, and $B=(S\otimes_k\Omega)_{\mathfrak q}$ [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. Then $\mathfrak q$ lies over $\mathfrak p$, $B/\mathfrak m_B=\Omega$, and there is an isomorphism of complete local $\Omega$-algebras $\widehat B\cong\Omega[[u,v]]/(uv)$.

source.place: Tags 0C49 (lemma-nodal-algebraic) and 0C4D (lemma-nodal), the algebraically closed quadratic coordinate change; Varieties Tag 0C54 (lemma-base-change-complete-local-ring) for scalar extension of the chosen presentation.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-separable-evaluation-local-base-change] with $K=\Omega$ and the specified $\iota$. Its evaluation map is exactly the map defining $\mathfrak q$ here; hence $\mathfrak q$ is maximal, contracts to $\mathfrak p$, and $B/\mathfrak qB\cong\Omega$ via evaluation. In particular $\mathfrak m_B=\mathfrak qB$, proving the first two assertions. The hypotheses are precisely finite generation of $S/k$, maximality of $\mathfrak p$, finite separability of $F/k$, and the chosen embedding.

source.place: Tags 0C4Y (lemma-change-fields-flat) and 0C50 (lemma-change-fields-algebraic-unramified), at the evaluation point.

proof.text: Invert the given continuous complete local $F$-algebra isomorphism to obtain the presentation $F[[u,v]]\twoheadrightarrow\widehat A$ with kernel $(Q)$. Its coefficients act through the given $k$-algebra section $\sigma$, and $Q\in(u,v)$ since it is homogeneous of degree two. Apply [lem-trf-field-extension-completion-presentation] with $K=\Omega$, $n=2$, and the single relation $Q$. It gives $\widehat B\cong\Omega[[u,v]]/(a_0u^2+b_0uv+c_0v^2)$ as complete local $\Omega$-algebras, where $a_0=\iota(a)$, $b_0=\iota(b)$ and $c_0=\iota(c)$. Since $\iota$ is injective, $\Delta_0=b_0^2-4a_0c_0=\iota(b^2-4ac)\ne0$.

source.place: Tag 0C54, lemma-base-change-complete-local-ring, chosen presentation after scalar extension.

source.place: Tag 0C4D, lemma-nodal, first proof paragraph: nondegenerate binary quadric is xy up to coordinates; explicit factorization.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-power-series-field-cohen-regular-complete] in its field case, $\Omega[[u,v]]$ and $\Omega[[U,V]]$ are complete for their variable maximal ideals. Since the $L_i$ lie in $(u,v)$, [lem-weil-pbc-power-series-universal-property-complete] gives an $\Omega$-algebra map $\phi:\Omega[[U,V]]\to\Omega[[u,v]]$ sending $(U,V)^{\mathsf T}$ to $M(u,v)^{\mathsf T}$. Apply the same universal property to the two linear forms $M^{-1}(U,V)^{\mathsf T}$ to obtain $\psi$ in the other direction. Both composites fix constants and each variable, since $M^{-1}M=MM^{-1}=1$; uniqueness in that universal property makes both composites the identity. These maps send every power of the variable ideal into the corresponding power, and so are continuous inverse local maps.

source.place: Tag 0C4D, lemma-nodal, first proof paragraph, linear coordinate change; power-series maps use more-algebra.tex Tag 07NL (lemma-power-series-ring-over-Cohen-fs), universal-property passage, and algebra.tex Tag 032C.

proof.text: Since $\phi(UV)=L_1L_2=Q_0$ and $\psi(Q_0)=UV$, the maps $\phi,\psi$ descend to mutually inverse $\Omega$-algebra maps $\Omega[[U,V]]/(UV)\cong\Omega[[u,v]]/(Q_0)$. Indeed multiples of the displayed generator map to multiples of the other generator, and the composites on quotient classes are the identity. They identify the variable maximal ideals, hence their powers, so this is an isomorphism of complete local $\Omega$-algebras. Compose its inverse with the isomorphism from step 2 and rename $U,V$ to $u,v$ to obtain the asserted $\widehat B\cong\Omega[[u,v]]/(uv)$.
